Group it by practicality, not just the fare difference.

Most practical: switch to the later connected return. It preserves the final clinic morning and gives you time to pack materials after the lot detour. I do not see a good middle option; standby or hoping the clinic ends early just moves the risk back to Thursday.
Switch it. The later arrival is annoying, but I need the course to end cleanly. Can you keep me in window seats and translate the parking map?

For materials after wrap, use the north service pull-off only after 12:30; the clinic contact will meet you there.
Set Thursday timing around that.

messages.content: Raleigh is wrapped, and I want to look at Amelia Island for a beach-and-bike reset in December. We’d drive from Tampa. Can you compare Friday-to-Monday versus shortening it?
Yes. Which December weekend, and should I include condos as well as hotels? Also tell me if there are any amenities that matter for this one so I do not rank it only by nightly rate.

Dec. 13 to 16 for two people. Include a resort, an inn, and a condo if the numbers are real. I care about total cost with taxes, parking, and resort fees, beach access, recent reviews, cancellation, queen or king bed, coffee and fridge, and pool/hot tub/fitness. Not just cheapest.

I found three realistic choices for Dec. 13-16. Amelia Shoreline Resort: beachfront, 4.6 recent guest score, cancellable queen coastal room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness center; about $1,064 all-in once tax, resort fee, and parking are included. Fernandina House Inn: historic district, 4.5, very walkable to dinners, queen room, coffee listed, fridge details inconsistent; about $712 all-in, parking included, but no pool, hot tub, or fitness room. Sea Oats condo: near Main Beach, 4.1 with fewer recent reviews, full kitchen and more space; about $1,018 all-in, pool listed, no hot tub, no clear fitness access, and stricter cancellation.
Group them by practicality and tell me what breaks on each one.

Least friction for beach and recovery: Amelia Shoreline Resort. You park once, walk straight to the beach, and have the hot tub/fitness setup after biking. What breaks: it is the highest hotel total, and dinners are less walkable. Best price plus dinner walkability: Fernandina House Inn. What breaks: the beach becomes a drive or longer bike, there is no recovery amenity set, and the fridge is not guaranteed in every room. Most space: Sea Oats condo. What breaks: fewer recent reviews, less flexible cancellation, and the fixed cleaning/service fees make it a weaker value if you shorten.
Is the resort total really all-in? I do not want parking or a resort fee appearing later.

For three nights, the resort math is $789 room, $104.38 tax, $105 resort fee, and $66 self-parking, so $1,064.38 total. The resort fee and parking are mandatory, not optional add-ons. The cancellable rate requires a one-night deposit and allows free cancellation until Dec. 6 at 4 p.m. Eastern. Breakfast is not included.
The inn is the only one close to dinners, right?

Yes. The inn is the easiest for meals: several restaurants are within a 5- to 10-minute walk in the historic district. The beach is about 1.3 miles away, so it is doable by bike but not a step-outside beach stay. The practical caveat is exactly what you flagged: no pool, no hot tub, no fitness room, and the mini-fridge wording says select rooms or request basis rather than guaranteed.
And the condo? I like having a kitchen, but not if the cancellation terms are a trap.

The condo gives you the best room setup: full kitchen, primary queen, second small bedroom, washer/dryer, and parking included. The caution is the commitment. It has a 48-hour free-cancel window after booking, then the service fee is nonrefundable, and it becomes nonrefundable inside 30 days. Reviews are fine but thinner than the hotels. It has a community pool, but no hot tub and no listed fitness access.
What do the two-night numbers look like?

Approximate two-night totals: Friday-Sunday would be resort $736, inn $486, condo $790. Saturday-Monday would be resort $741, inn $489, condo $795. The condo does not shorten well because cleaning and service fees stay fixed. Dropping one night saves the resort cost, but you either lose the easy Friday arrival or the quiet Monday morning.
If we can leave Friday morning, is Monday worth the extra night?

I think yes, if the total is acceptable. Friday arrival gives you time for a small grocery stop, check-in, and a beach walk without making Saturday absorb the travel fatigue. Saturday can be the bike day, Sunday can flex for weather or a lighter ride, and Monday can stay calm before the drive home. Friday-Sunday gives you only one full day. Saturday-Monday makes Saturday both travel and settling-in.
The inn price is tempting, but missing hot tub and uncertain fridge are not tiny for this trip.

That is the main trade-off. The inn saves roughly $350 compared with the resort for three nights and wins on restaurant walkability, but it gives up the recovery setup and a reliable room routine. If you stayed there, you would likely drive for beach time and still need to confirm cold storage.
What would you choose if the goal is low-friction recovery, not fancy?

If Friday morning departure is realistic, I would book the refundable Amelia Shoreline Resort Friday-Monday. It costs more, but it removes the daily beach-drive friction and gives you the better post-activity setup. If Friday falls apart, I would not force the condo; I would either choose the cheaper inn for a shorter stay with the missing-amenity caveat or postpone.
Do not book yet. My partner needs to confirm Friday. Save the resort and set a rate check. Also note the caveats so I can ask him cleanly.

Saved. There is no courtesy hold available, so I set a six-day rate and availability check plus a reminder before the free-cancel window. Ask him three things: can we leave Tampa by about 8:30 Friday, are we comfortable with the $1,064.38 all-in total including mandatory resort and parking fees, and are we okay driving or ridesharing for some dinners? If yes, the practical choice is the beachfront resort Friday-Monday. If no, the inn is the cheaper fallback, with no pool, hot tub, or fitness room and fridge details to confirm.

Booked. Confirmation ASR-48172, Dec. 13-16, queen coastal-view room, cancellable until Dec. 6 at 4 p.m. Eastern. The one-night deposit was charged to the card on file, and the remaining balance, including the resort and parking fees, is due at the hotel.
Now give me the Friday drive plan from Tampa. I want the grocery stop before check-in, but not a giant errand.

Friday plan: leave Tampa around 8:30 a.m., keep one easy rest stop, and aim for Fernandina Beach early afternoon. Do a small Publix stop on Sadler Road before the resort: drinks, breakfast items, ride snacks, and anything for the mini-fridge. Then go to the resort around 2:30-3:00. If the room is not ready, leave bags with the desk and do a short beach walk until check-in opens.
Let’s not pretend we’ll bike after that drive. Beach walk only Friday.

Agreed. Friday is drive, small grocery stop, check-in, easy beach walk, and hot tub if the hours work. Dinner can be a short drive into Fernandina or something simple near the resort; no ride plan that day.
What is the Saturday plan if the weather is ugly?

Plan A if dry: an easy Amelia Island Trail and Fort Clinch ride, roughly 12-15 miles with options to cut it shorter. Low-weather backup: Fort Clinch visitor center and short paved sections between showers, Amelia Island Museum of History, coffee or lunch in the historic district, resort fitness center, and pool or hot tub time if open. If it is windy rather than rainy, keep the ride shorter and avoid exposed beach-road stretches.
Keep Monday unrushed.

Monday stays loose: in-room coffee, slow packing, beach walk around 8:30, checkout about 10:45, depart around 11:00, lunch stop near Gainesville or Ocala, and Tampa arrival roughly 3:45-4:30 depending on traffic. No early alarm and no planned Monday activity that makes the drive feel tight.
Add reminders for cancellation, checking hot tub hours, and bike gear.

Done. Reminders are set for Dec. 5 to review the booking before the Dec. 6 cancellation cutoff, the week before travel to confirm hot tub and fitness center hours plus parking instructions, and Thursday evening to pack helmets, bike locks, lights, flat kit, cooler, and simple breakfast/snacks. Amelia Island is booked Friday-Monday, with the return drive deliberately unrushed.
